citations.B1: Check-then-set race: two threads can both read `count < limit` and both increment
citations.B2: both increment, so users exceed the limit and increments are lost
citations.B3: guard with a `threading.Lock` (or an atomic INCR in a shared store)
citations.B4: No time window: counts never reset, so `limit` is a lifetime quota
citations.B5: Unbounded memory: the dict grows with every distinct `user_id` forever
citations.B6: Per-process state: each worker has its own `counts`, so the real limit is `limit × workers`
citations.B7: No input validation: unhashable `user_id` raises `TypeError` and `None` becomes a shared bucket
